text:
The proposal failed the check, so I sent `mastermind-auth-merge` a rewrite of `requirements.md` and logged it as `sent` in `flags.jsonl`. I haven't confirmed the agent applied it.

`text-check.mjs` came back clean. The failure was the first paragraph, about 120 words against the 60-word limit, which described the file structure in sentences instead of drawing it. The rewrite replaces it with a folder tree, a stages checklist, a constraints list and a tickable acceptance list.

I've written the review, and the verdict is **fix**. The work does what the owner asked, but some older docs still name files that were deleted. The report is at `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/15/spawned/mastermind-auth-merge/review.md`.

**What's met:**
- One Worker now serves `public/` and `/api/*`.
- The old `app/` code was moved into `worker/`, the demo UI is in `public/app/`, and `DocStore` is in `core/Item/`.
- Staging and production are separate environments in one config file, each with its own database.
- The root `wrangler.jsonc` still serves static files only, and the API answers only on listed hostnames (503 anywhere else), so a push or a preview url can't reach production data.
- Production hasn't been cut over.

**Tests:** I ran the four tests that need no server and they pass. I didn't re-run `api.test.mjs` because it needs a running stage; the session log says it covered all 15 routes.

**The two fixes (stale docs):**
1. `public/imagine/platform/decisions/local-dev.md` still describes `wrangler.dev.jsonc` and `worker/schema.sql`, which no longer exist, and `dev.mjs` still points readers to it.
2. The same old names appear in `identity.md`, `cms/d1/doc/decisions.md`, `platform/readme.md`, `slice.md` and `platform/local/page.js`. Each needs a one-line pointer to the new files.

**Notes worth a look:**
- Real Google sign-in has never run. Every stage has an empty `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, so "staging verified" only covers sign-ins faked with signed test cookies, and the readme no longer says so.
- Banning only works with the local dev login; nothing on staging or production can ban a real user.
- Once this reaches `main`, lew42.com will serve `/app/` with no API behind it: a login page that can't sign anyone in.
- `deploy.mjs` deploys before it creates `SESSION_SECRET`, so the first production deploy would briefly fail every sign-in.
- Smaller gaps: `DocStore` has no core test, nothing shows live `Room` instances, and the old `ADMIN_GOOGLE_SUB` option was dropped without a mention.

I made no code edits.

The verdict is **fix**. The merge does what the owner asked, but three things need changing before it's done. The report is in `mastermind-auth-merge/review.md`.

**What's met:** one Worker now serves `public/` and answers `/api/*`, with staging and production configured separately. The old `app/` code is ported and deleted. The four tests that need no server pass (I ran them). Pushing to git still can't put the API on lew42.com, and preview URLs get a 503 from the API. I didn't run `api.test.mjs`, because it needs a running stage.

**The three fixes:**
- **Old local-dev docs:** `local-dev.md` (which `dev.mjs` points readers to) still names `wrangler.dev.jsonc` and `worker/schema.sql`, which were deleted.
- **Other stale names:** five more docs still use the old file names. I searched the worktree again and they're all still there.
- **Bucket name mismatch:** the readme tells the owner to create a production R2 bucket called `monorepo-docs`, but the comment in `wrangler.jsonc` gives the pattern `monorepo-<stage>-docs`, i.e. `monorepo-production-docs`.

**Worth a look (notes):**
- Real Google sign-in has never run, because the Google client ID is empty on every stage. The readme doesn't say so.
- Banning a user only works with the local dev login.
- When this merges and reaches `main`, lew42.com will serve the `/app/` page with no API behind it. That shows a login page that can't sign anyone in, before the announced cutover.
- The first production deploy will fail sign-ins briefly, because the script deploys before it creates the session secret.
- `DocStore` has no test, and there is no page that lists live documents or their editing locks.
- The readme has one sentence in an agent's first person ("My API token…").
- `public/app.js` (the site's own entry file) and the new `public/app/` folder sit side by side, which is easy to confuse.

This replaced an earlier review of the same diff, which was written into this same `review.md`. Its findings are still in `review.jsonl`. I made no code edits.

The verdict is **fix**, but for one stale line, not a design problem. I made no code edits.

**The fix:** `worker/readme.md` still lists "a `DocStore` test" under "Not built yet". That test now exists, and I ran it in the worktree: 9 checks, all passed. Remove those words so a fresh agent doesn't write the test a second time.

**Notes (no action required):**
- **Wording:** `identity.md:64` calls `dev.js` "the `main` of `worker/wrangler.jsonc`", but that file now has a `main` for every stage, so the sentence reads as if it contradicts itself. It should say "the local stage's `main`".
- **No live-instance page:** nothing shows the open documents and who holds each lock. The readme already lists this as not built.
- **Wide screens:** `/imagine/platform/local/` is 57% empty at 3440. That was already true before this change, which only edited one sentence on the page.

**Earlier rounds' findings are all fixed:**
- The old file names in the docs are gone.
- The R2 bucket names now match between the readme and the config.
- The deploy script creates the session secret before it deploys.
- `/app/` on a host with no API now says so and doesn't register a service worker.
- The readme no longer speaks as an agent ("my token").
- The readme's "Not built yet" section now covers Google sign-in and bans.

**Requirements and indexing:** all 14 asks are met or tracked. Production cutover is still a separate step, as planned. The four pure worker tests pass; I didn't run `api.test.mjs` because it needs a running stage. Every new file is indexed. A fresh agent could continue from the task folder alone, apart from the stale line above.

Screenshots were at 400, 1200, 1920 and 3440 for the one page the diff touched.

The full report is at `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/15/spawned/mastermind-auth-merge/review/report.md`.

I checked the local-api-proxy proposal and found nothing to rewrite. `node Server/text-check.mjs` printed no flags. The task dir holds only `requirements.md`, which is written for agents, so there is no owner-facing text yet to judge. I didn't screenshot anything, since there is no page.

I logged one "clear" line in `.claude/skills/clarity/flags.jsonl`.

**Verdict: fix.** One finding is a blocker; the report is at `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/15/spawned/mastermind-auth-merge/local-api-proxy/review.md`.

### Must change
- **Servex would not start after this merge.** `Servex/Servex.js:436` has `replace(//$/, "")`. The backslash is missing, so `//` starts a comment and `node --check Servex/Servex.js` fails with a syntax error. It should be `/\/$/`. The new `ReverseProxy.test.mjs` doesn't load Servex.js, so it could not catch this. I also couldn't run that test in the worktree: it has no `node_modules`, so `http-proxy` is missing.
- **The checks through `monorepo.localhost` haven't been run.** So far the Worker has only been tested on a private port with a forged Host header. Still to check through the real proxy: dev login, `/app/`, `live.test.mjs`, live reload, rpc writes, folder names and the page index.
- **The 3–5 line message to voice-app hasn't been sent.**
- **`public/app/readme.md:5` is out of date.** It still sends readers to `localhost:8787`; the normal address is now `http://monorepo.localhost/app/`.

### Worth a look
- `ai/cards/card.js:680` fetches a bare `/api/objects`, which belongs to Servex. On `monorepo.localhost` that request now reaches the Worker and starts wrangler for nothing.
- The proxy waits 15 s for a starting service, but wrangler took about 17 s to boot. So the first request from `/app/` will probably get a 503; check that the page recovers.
- The dev login now accepts any `*.localhost` host name. That's safe given the local `API_HOSTS` list.

### What's sound
- The design is simple and generic: the routes are config in the project's own `package.json`, and each one becomes a second Servex project. Nothing is special-cased for the monorepo.
- `GET /api/` lists the endpoints from the ROUTES table, as asked.
- All callers of the old `/api/folder-names` and `/api/index` moved to the new `/dev/` paths.
- None of the newly ignored asset paths are tracked in git.
- A fresh agent could pick this up from the task folder alone.
